title: Datascene/VAA1 Data Book Publication Package
description: Canonical schema for browsable per-video publication packages and whole-corpus publication packages. Each operational feature publishes one governed Data Book chapter per video, including governed empty states. Natural-language reports cite eligible Data Book claims at sentence level. Corpus packages preserve video identity, source clocks, versions, authority, associated files, and comparison matrices.

x-datascene-semantic-rules.description: For every video, the set of Data Book chapter feature_id values must equal the set of registry entries whose publication_status is operational and whose publication_scope includes per_video.
Each operational feature may publish exactly one canonical chapter per video and edition. Alternative views must reference that chapter rather than create competing publications.
A chapter with no publishable records must use a governed empty content_state and provide an empty_state object. A bare empty records array is insufficient.

Every empirical or interpretive report sentence must cite one or more eligible Data Book claims. Each citation must resolve to a chapter, record or claim, evidence reference, and source coordinates or an explicit source-unavailable state.
A report may not cite claims whose eligibility status is ineligible, withdrawn, superseded, privacy_blocked, or validation_failed.

A corpus package must contain or reference exactly one preserved video publication for every included video. Video identifiers, source clocks, chapter versions, and authority contexts must not be flattened or silently merged.
Every associated file and archive entry marked included must have a valid checksum. Canonical serialization and path ordering must produce deterministic content identity.

A published, archived, or superseded edition must pass the lifecycle chain: generate, persist, reopen, export, checksum verification, report sentence resolution, Data Book record resolution, and source-evidence resolution.
